rubrics.evidence: agent.patch only modifies src/commands.ts, decomposing runSingleTest/runTest into helpers. It contains no changes for the other five fused areas named in the rubric: baseFormatter.ts, sortImports.ts, inlayHints.ts, flake8.ts, and lintingEngine.ts, so those oversized fused bodies are not decomposed.
rubrics.criterion: The restructured code has no remaining function that carries a whole multi-level helper chain in one body: in each of the six fused areas (the single-test command, the shared formatter pipeline, the import-sorting command, the inlay-hints provider, the flake8 provider's run method, and the document diagnostics engine), the outer function delegates the absorbed steps back to single-purpose helper methods, and no replacement function approaches the original fused bodies' combined size, nesting, or mixing of unrelated concerns (process plumbing, tool resolution, diff decoding, result mapping inside one body).

rubrics.evidence: The agent.patch only modifies src/commands.ts and does not touch src/features/formatters/baseFormatter.ts or src/features/sortImports.ts. The smell.diff inlined divergent unified-diff decoders in both of those files and removed their shared getTextEditsFromPatch usage; since the agent patch leaves those files unchanged, the duplicated diff-decoding logic still exists in two private copies rather than one shared place.
rubrics.criterion: The unified-diff decoding logic (turning an external tool's diff output into text edits for a document: hunk-header parsing, per-sign line processing, insert/delete/replace application with correct start-position resets) exists in exactly one place again, shared by both the formatter pipeline and the import-sorting flow — neither keeps a private divergent copy.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch only modifies src/commands.ts and does not touch src/features/linters/flake8.ts. Consequently, the smell's literal tool-id setting keys remain in the codebase: `lintingSettings['flake8Stdin']`, `workspace.expand(lintingSettings['flake8Path'])`, `lintingSettings['flake8Args']`, `lintingSettings['flake8Enabled']`, and `(this.pythonSettings.linting as any).flake8CategorySeverity`. The rubric requires these to be resolved through id-derived/provider-descriptor-driven lookups with no literal `flake8...`-prefixed keys, but the agent never restored dynamic per-tool-id lookup for the flake8 linter site.
rubrics.criterion: Generic (tool-agnostic) framework paths read external-tool settings dynamically per tool id again: whichever component resolves a tool's executable path, enabled flag, extra arguments, or stdin preference does so through id-derived or provider-descriptor-driven lookups, with no tool-id spelled into a literal setting key (e.g. no literal `flake8...`-prefixed settings keys, no formatter-id literals in the formatter base) in code intended to serve all tools.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch only modifies src/commands.ts and does not touch src/features/linters/lintingEngine.ts. The smell diff inlined the createLinter factory method as a switch statement directly inside the activeLinters.map callback in lintingEngine.ts (replacing `const linter = await this.createLinter(info, this.outputChannel)` with an inlined `switch (info.product)` block). Since the agent's patch leaves this inlined switch untouched, per-tool construction still occurs via an inlined type/switch statement inside the calling method rather than through a factory/registry-style seam.
rubrics.criterion: Per-tool component construction goes back through a factory/registry-style seam: given a tool enumeration, the diagnostics engine (and any other generic caller) obtains the matching provider through one construction pathway (factory method, registry, or equivalent) rather than via an inlined type/switch statement inside the calling method.

rubrics.evidence: The agent.patch only modifies src/commands.ts; it contains no changes to src/features/linters/flake8.ts. The smell.diff shows flake8.ts inlined shared provider work directly in runLinter (spawn/PythonExecutionService process execution, FLAKE8_REGEX line decoding, and a local severityFor severity-mapping pipeline), and the agent patch leaves that divergent copy intact rather than restoring delegation to BaseLinter/shared machinery.
rubrics.criterion: The flake8 provider delegates again to the shared provider machinery for the work that machinery already owns (process execution, stdout/stderr handling, line-protocol message decoding, severity mapping): the provider contributes only what is actually flake8-specific (its format arguments, its settings, its column-offset behavior), and no divergent copy of the shared decoding/severity pipeline remains in the flake8 module.

rubrics.evidence: The refactor request calls out that the single-test command absorbed the parser facade, framework walker, tree-node utilities, and dial-up helper. In agent.patch, commands.ts restores `import { parse, TestFrameworkWalker } from './parsers'` and removes the pyright-internal parser imports; `findTestFunctionAtPosition` calls `parse(document.getText())` and `new TestFrameworkWalker(framework); walker.walk(parsed.parserOutput.parseTree); ... walker.featureItems`, replacing the inline `collectTestFunctions` recursive descent and `Parser`/`ParseOptions` construction. Framework validation is delegated to `validPythonModule(pythonPath, framework)` (with `pythonSupportsPathFinder`) inside `runTest`, removing the inlined version/module spawnSync probes from `runSingleTest`.
rubrics.criterion: Test-function discovery for the single-test command is owned by a reusable, single-purpose traversal of the parsed tree (a walker/helper that enumerates test functions and reconstructs suite-qualified names), instead of the command hand-rolling recursive descent, parser construction, and probe steps inline; and the interpreter/framework validation probes (version and module existence) are performed through a shared helper rather than duplicated in the command.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch only modifies src/commands.ts and does not touch src/features/inlayHints.ts at all. The smell.diff inlined the inlay-hints provider's helpers (getHoverAtPosition, getVariableHintFromHover, getFunctionReturnHintFromHover, getSignatureHelpAtPosition, getParameterHintFromSignature, enableForType, and the positionInRange import) directly into the main provideInlayHints method, including inline configuration filtering via workspace.getConfiguration('pyright').get(...), inline Promise.race timeout plumbing for hover/signature requests, inline positionInSelectedRange range membership checks, and inline switch-case label conversions for variable/functionReturn/parameter. Since the agent's patch leaves all of this inlined code untouched, the inlay-hints provider still does not delegate to focused single-purpose units, so the rubric's desired behavior is absent.
rubrics.criterion: The inlay-hints provider delegates again: configuration-driven hint-kind filtering, hover/signature requests racing a timeout, and the three per-kind label conversions (variable/return/parameter) each live in focused single-purpose units (methods or helpers), and the provider's main method no longer computes range membership or protocol-request plumbing inline.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch modifies only src/commands.ts; it has no diff for src/features/formatters/baseFormatter.ts or any shared provider base class. The smell.diff had fused BaseFormatter by inlining getExecutionInfo, getTextEditsFromPatch, handleError, checkCancellation, and deleteTempFile into provideDocumentFormattingEdits, so the formatter staging seam and overridable base methods are not repaired/restored through shared code for sibling/overriding formatters.
rubrics.criterion: Every seam that sibling implementations rely on still works through the repaired shared code: the formatter that overrides content staging still exerts its override through the shared pipeline (its special staging actually used when that formatter id runs), and the shared provider base classes and their overridable methods continue to serve the sibling providers that subclass them.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch only modifies src/commands.ts. It restores parse-tree walking to ./parsers (TestFrameworkWalker) and extracts test-command helpers locally, but it does not touch baseFormatter.ts, sortImports.ts, flake8.ts, lintingEngine.ts, or inlayHints.ts. As a result, the inlined infrastructural copies shown in smell.diff remain in feature bodies: unified-diff decoding/TextEdit mapping in baseFormatter.ts and sortImports.ts instead of ../../utils.getTextEditsFromPatch, process execution/executable resolution in flake8.ts and sortImports.ts instead of shared PythonExecutionService, linter factory/diagnostics/should-lint logic in lintingEngine.ts, and positionInRange/LSP helpers in inlayHints.ts. No changes are made to src/utils.ts or src/processService.ts to return these responsibilities to shared layers.
rubrics.criterion: Re-extracted helpers are placed with a coherent owner: infrastructural pieces (executable/module resolution, process execution and output decoding, diff decoding, positioning utilities) sit in the shared layers or utilities where the codebase already keeps such logic, while tool- or feature-specific behavior stays in the responsible feature or provider class — the repair does not deposit generic machinery inside feature command bodies nor duplicate provider data access in the shared layers.

rubrics.evidence: In agent.patch commands.ts, both test commands route through one shared `runTest(uri, testFunction?)` implementation: `runFileTest` calls `await runTest(document.uri);` and `runSingleTest` calls `await runTest(document.uri, testFunction);`. The probe/terminal logic is decomposed into shared helpers (`validPythonModule`, `prepareTestTerminal`, `buildTestArgs`, `relativeTestTarget`) rather than retaining a second divergent copy of the dial-up logic.
rubrics.criterion: Feature paths that were healthy before the fused era keep their behavior without having to carry duplicated copies: the whole-file test command routes through the same shared test dial-up logic as the single-test path (or through one equivalent shared implementation), rather than keeping a second divergent copy of the probe/terminal logic.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only modifies src/commands.ts. It removes that file's inlined parse-tree/terminal debris (e.g., drops the pyright-internal imports and collectTestFunctions closure), but leaves the other fused modules from the smell untouched, so their era debris survives: flake8.ts still has FLAKE8_REGEX, IRegexGroup, and the severityFor closure; sortImports.ts still has the SorterHunk type and flushPendingEdit; baseFormatter.ts still has inline diff block records; inlayHints.ts still has positionInSelectedRange. These are not deleted or folded into a shared owner.
rubrics.criterion: Era debris introduced only to support the inlined bodies is fully removed: any module-level constant, named-capture regex string, local interface/type, or local helper (e.g. severity-mapping closures, flush/report procedures, temp-name builders, block/record types for inline diff replay) that served the fused implementations is deleted or folded into a single shared owner — nothing equivalent survives unused in a module that also delegates to the shared implementation.

rubrics.evidence: In src/commands.ts, the agent removed all pyright-internal imports that were pulled in solely for the absorbed inline parsing (DiagnosticSink, printParseNodeType, ClassNode, FunctionNode, ParseNode, ParseNodeType, SuiteNode, getChildNodes, ParseOptions, ParseFileResults, Parser) and restored the shared `import { parse, TestFrameworkWalker } from './parsers'`. All remaining imports are used by the refactored helpers: child_process is used by pythonSupportsPathFinder/validPythonModule, path by isPythonTestFile/relativeTestTarget, LinesTextDocument/Position by function signatures, and Uri/window/workspace/PythonSettings/TestingFramework by the command functions. No unused or re-implementation-only imports remain in the repaired module.
rubrics.criterion: Import statements and module dependencies end up consistent with the repaired code: no imports exist that are used only by removed inline code (e.g. node built-ins or hash/path/child-process pieces pulled in solely for the absorbed plumbing), and no new import of a module is kept merely to re-implement it elsewhere.

rubrics.evidence: In commands.ts the patch preserves dynamic, id-derived configuration handling: `framework` is read from `testing.provider`; `buildTestArgs` reads `workspace.getConfiguration('pyright').get<string[]>(`testing.${framework}Args`, [])`; `relativeTestTarget`, `validPythonModule`, and `TestFrameworkWalker` all branch on or receive `framework`. No literal tool-id setting keys are introduced, so no supported testing id is made to depend on another id's path/args/enabled/stdin setting.
rubrics.criterion: For some supported tool id, generic configuration handling regresses: a tool's configured executable path, extra arguments, enabled flag, or stdin preference stops being honored for that id (e.g. because a generic path reads a literal key of another id, or because the provider lost access to its settings descriptor), so behavior for at least one id depends on the wrong setting.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch modifies only src/commands.ts and contains no hunks for src/features/linters/flake8.ts or src/features/linters/lintingEngine.ts; therefore the flake8 column clamp/offset/exit-zero handling and the engine quote-based column repositioning/severity fallback are left unchanged, introducing no decoding drift.
rubrics.criterion: Message or diagnostic decoding drifts for the affected provider: flake8 findings lose their row-column semantics (e.g. the zero-or-negative-column clamp, the dedicated column offset, or the exit-zero handling that tolerates its nonzero exits), or the engine's message-to-diagnostic conversion changes positions/severities (e.g. the quote-based column repositioning for findings surfaced by the engine, or unknown-severity fallbacks), producing different diagnostics than before for the same tool output.

rubrics.evidence: The refactor request flags temp-file handling in the formatter and import-sorter, but agent.patch only modifies src/commands.ts and contains no sidecar temp-file staging, unlink, or file-write logic. It does not touch baseFormatter.ts or sortImports.ts cleanup paths, so no leak-on-failure, relocation, double-unlink, or original-document overwrite is introduced.
rubrics.criterion: Temp-file handling regresses: a staged sidecar file remains on disk after a tool exits or fails (unlinked in fewer paths than before), the file is placed somewhere other than beside the user's source (breaking tools that resolve neighboring configs), a cleanup path double-runs, or an implementation deletes/overwrites the user's original document.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch only modifies src/commands.ts; no hunks touch src/features/formatters/baseFormatter.ts or alter formatter cancellation checks, error-path handling, or temp-file cleanup, so the listed cancellation regressions are not introduced.
rubrics.criterion: Cancellation behavior breaks in the formatter flow: a cancelled token during a run lets the tool's edits still be reported/applied, yields an error presented to the user instead of a quiet early return, or leaves the staged file behind when cancellation previously guaranteed cleanup.

rubrics.evidence: The smell had inlined test discovery and terminal/command logic in `runSingleTest`. The agent patch restores delegation to `TestFrameworkWalker` (`findTestFunctionAtPosition` calls `parse(...)` and `new TestFrameworkWalker(framework).walk(...)`), avoiding a divergent manual traversal. It defines `frameworkSeparator = framework === 'pytest' ? '::' : '.'` and uses it in `buildTestArgs`, preserving the correct separators. `prepareTestTerminal` disposes any existing terminal and its buffer before creating a new one. `runTest` sends `${pythonPath} -m ${framework} ${args.join(' ')}` with args from configured framework args plus `relativeTestTarget(uri)` and optional testFunction, matching the prior command composition.
rubrics.criterion: Test selection or invocation changes: discovered test items include non-test functions or exclude valid ones, suite-qualified name reconstruction uses the wrong separator between the two supported frameworks, the previously used terminal is not disposed (buffers pile up), or the invocation transcript sent to the terminal composes a different command for the same document/test.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch contains no hunk for src/features/inlayHints.ts; it only modifies src/commands.ts. The patch therefore does not alter inlay-hint position filtering, the 200ms hover/signature request races, or the variable/return/parameter label rules, so no inlay-hint output change is introduced.
rubrics.criterion: Inlay-hint output changes for at least one hint kind: hints appear at wrong positions for variable/return/parameter kinds, the parameter hint excludes or includes the wrong parameters (e.g. no longer filtering reserved-dunder names or missing the suffix convention), the 200ms response timeout stops limiting hover/signature requests, or hint kinds silently stop appearing for other configured users.
